doctrine: The Pixel IS its own Circle of Willis — redundant blood supply for the Diamond Lens. If one path blocks, another opens. ALL paths are life paths.

1_adb_wifi.reliability: fragile — Android kills adbd on screen lock, needs auth dialog
1_adb_wifi.fix: Pixel must have 'Always allow from this computer' checked + developer options 'Stay awake' ON

2_adb_usb.reliability: solid — physical cable, no WiFi drops
what_flows: everything ADB WiFi does + faster transfers
2_adb_usb.fix: Plug USB-C from eastGate to Pixel

3_wifi_http.reliability: moderate — WiFi can drop, IP changes
3_wifi_http.fix: Start HTTP services on Pixel: llama-server, biomeOS serve, sensor-http

4_bluetooth.fix: Pair eastGate BT with Pixel, create rfcomm serial bridge or BLE GATT sensor service

5_rss_outbound.endpoint: Pixel generates feed.xml, eastGate pulls via HTTP
5_rss_outbound.reliability: high — no persistent connection needed, pull-based
5_rss_outbound.fix: Create a tiny HTTP server on Pixel that serves sensor data as RSS/JSON

6_nfc_tap.fix: Android NFC beam or HCE service for gate-to-gate config

7_cellular_sms.fix: Build SMS-to-command bridge: southGate receives SMS → forwards to Pixel via IP

willis_policy.emergency: rss_outbound (pull-based, works even if Pixel can't accept connections)
willis_policy.last_resort: cellular_sms (works even if WiFi is completely dead)

circle_rule: ANY path that flows is a life path. The Pixel should ALWAYS have at least 2 paths open. If ADB is stuck, HTTP still works. If WiFi drops, BT beacons. If everything network dies, SMS through southGate. The organism adapts — it doesn't depend on one artery.
